S34.02.needs: a Free or paid account with more than 10 saved chats (the search box is hidden below 10)
S34.02.note: The search box only appears when there are more than 10 chats; the code matches title and message text in filterConversations.
steps: Sign in and make sure the account has saved chats.
Click the clock icon in the top header; its label is "Recent chats".
If the account has more than 10 chats, click the search box "Search recent chats" and type a word from a chat title.
Check that only chats with a matching title are listed.
Clear the box, then type a word that appears only inside a message body (not the title) and check that its chat is listed.
Click the matching chat and check that it opens.
S34.02.where: Header clock icon (Recent chats) > Search recent chats

S34.06.needs: an outside account (Google, Slack or Notion) and a paid or entitled account where connectors are available
S34.06.note: The search itself runs on the server during the chat; the side panel only links to the connectors page. The code at side_panel.ts:8133 has moved, so this path comes from the + menu code near side_panel.ts:14818.
steps: Sign in and click the + button (its label is "Add attachment").
Click "Connectors"; a new tab opens on the web connectors page. If a "coming soon" tag shows, the item does nothing.
On that page, connect Drive, Slack or Notion.
Return to the side panel, start a new chat and ask a question about content in a connected source.
Look for an answer that cites the connected source, shown as a "sources" line under the answer.

S34.07.needs: a signed-in account whose routed model supports web search (which plans get it is unknown from the code)
S34.07.note: No web-search toggle was found in the extension; web search is turned on by the routed model's capability (managedChatHandler.ts:781), and the "Web search" label is only a model-list filter.
steps: Sign in and start a new chat.
Ask a question that needs current public information, such as today's news.
Look for an answer that uses web results and shows sources under it ("N sources").
S34.07.where: An answer in any chat to a question about current events

S34.23.needs: a chat answer that has citations (web search or connected sources)
S34.23.note: Previews appear only when the source has a title or snippet; the card is built in sources.ts buildSourceLink.
steps: Sign in and open an answer that cites sources (a chip shows a site name, such as "example.com", or "site +2").
Move the mouse over the chip (or tap it on a phone-width panel).
Check that a card appears with each source's site, title and, when present, a snippet and date.
Compare the card with the list under "N sources" to confirm the preview lines match.
S34.23.where: Answer text > source chip (site name with +N) > hover or tap

S34.24.needs: a chat answer that has sources
S34.24.note: The cards in the code are in sources.ts (buildSourceLink and buildCitationChip).
steps: Open an answer that has sources; wait until it finishes streaming, because the footer is hidden while streaming.
Look for the line "N sources" under the answer.
Click "N sources" to open the list, or hover a citation chip to open its card.
Check that each card or row shows the site, the title and a link.
S34.24.where: Answer > "N sources" (under the answer) > source rows

S34.26.needs: a chat answer that has sources
S34.26.note: The footer lists the answer's sources; sources consulted during agent steps appear in the step list (bubbles.ts appendActivitySources), which was not checked against "consulted" in Expected.
steps: Open an answer that has a "N sources" line under it.
Click "N sources"; the line is a disclosure and opens the full list.
Check that the list is labelled "Sources used for this answer" and shows each source.
Click "N sources" again and check that the list closes.

S34.27.needs: a chat answer that has sources
S34.27.note: Source links open with target _blank in sources.ts; the cited markdown.ts:122 is a sanitizer setting, not a control, and the agent-step source links in bubbles.ts (around line 866) were not checked live.
steps: Open an answer that has sources.
Click a citation chip, or click "N sources" and then a source title.
Check that a new browser tab opens.
Compare the new tab's address with the source's site shown on the card.
S34.27.where: Answer > "N sources" > source title, or a citation chip

S34.32.needs: a Free or paid account; the unavailable-source case needs an organisation site policy that cannot be read, which a tester cannot set up
S34.32.note: Empty states for chat history are confirmed; the unavailable-source messages ("Your organization’s site policy could not be read, so history was not searched." in historySearch.ts, and "Browsing history could not be searched." in side_panel.ts) are not checked live and the connector path was not reproduced.
steps: Sign in with at least one saved chat and click the clock icon labelled "Recent chats".
If the account has more than 10 chats, click "Search recent chats" and type text that matches nothing, such as a random word.
Check that the list shows "No matching conversations" instead of an empty area.
For an account with no saved chats, check that the list shows "No saved conversations".
S34.32.where: Recent chats (clock icon) > Search recent chats
